newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-CUP TIES COULD BRING DOWN SPANISH MANAGERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CUP TIES COULD BRING DOWN SPANISH MANAGERS.

text.p: Managerial heads could roll this week in Spain as the third round of the Spanish Cup gets underway.

Although clubs still involved in European competition are excluded, three of the top four league teams will nevertheless be involved, amongst them league leaders Real Madrid, who face a tough draw against surprise outfit Valladolid.
The two-leg encounter comes just over a fortnight after the two sides drew 1-1 in the league.

Fabio Capello's side must play the second leg away from home and may line up for Thursday's game without captain Manolo Sanchis and German goalkeeper Bodo Illgner, both of whom have missed training through illness.
The game will not be a life-or-death struggle for Capello, but the same could hardly be said at Espanyol, where coach Pepe Carcelen offered his resignation at the weekend.

Carcelen was backed by the Espanyol board on Monday, but was warned that the club would take "appropriate measures" if the team lost in the Cup game against Sporting Gijon, where former Real Madrid manager Benito Floro is also under fire.
Former Espanyol coach Jose Antonio Camacho has already offered his resignation to the board at his new team, Sevilla, and will be desperately hoping for a result against Deportivo Coruna.
Injured Brazilian striker Bebeto will miss the the game against his old club, where manager John Toshack could himself do with a boost in the competition that Deportivo won in 1995.
The same is true of 1994 winners Zaragoza, who went on to take the 1995 European Cup Winners' Cup but are currently struggling at 18th in the league. Zaragoza take on mid-table Racing Santander.
Third round matches(first named teams play opening leg at home).
